reasoning: A graph on 9 vertices with girth ≥7 can contain at most a single 7‑cycle; any additional edges needed to raise every vertex’s degree to at least 3 would either create chords in that 7‑cycle (producing 3‑ or 4‑cycles) or connect the remaining two vertices in a way that creates a shorter cycle. Hence no graph satisfies both the degree bounds (3–6) and the girth requirement.
cot_trace: We need existence. 9 vertices, min degree 3 => total degree >=27, max degree 6 => total degree <=54, edges = sum/2 between 13.5 and 27 => at least 14 edges. Need girth >=7, so no cycles of length <=6. With 9 vertices, a graph with girth >=7 is essentially a forest plus maybe a 7-cycle. But 7-cycle uses 7 vertices, leaves 2 vertices attached without creating short cycles. Can we have min degree 3? Hard. A 7-cycle each vertex degree 2, need raise to >=3 by adding chords but chords create 3-4 cycles. So likely impossible. So UNSAT.
